full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: Defendant 10 has preferred this appeal challenging judgment and final decree dated 10-7-2019 passed by the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka accepting the Commissioner's report pursuant to judgment and decree dated 28-6-2007 passed in Title Suit 177 of 2005 decreeing the suit in preliminary form and granting separate saham to defendant 10. 

 2. Respondent as plaintiff filed Title Suit 151 of 2000 before the Subordinate Judge, Court No. 4, Dhaka on 25-6-2000 and the suit was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka on 28-8-2005 and renumbered as Title Suit 177 of 2005. Suit was filed for declaration of title with respect to 'Kha' schedule land and a decree to the effect that the Heba-bil-Ewaz document 7027 dated 15-8-1990 executed by Alimunnessa in respect of 1:--ha' schedule land is fraudulent, illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff and also for a decree of partition with regard to schedule land by evicting defendant 10. A further prayer to the effect that the Heba-bil-Ewaz document dated 2-3-2002 is actually inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff was added by amendment dated 27-7-2002. 

 3. This suit was heard analogously with Title Suits 180 and 183 of 2005 which were filed by contesting defendants 3 and 4 respectively. Both the suits were filed for permanent injunction. 

 4. The case of the plaintiffs is that the 'Ka' schedule partible land measuring 0.74 acres of CS plots 4613 and 4614 belonged to CS tenants Lai Mia @ Miah Helu and Kalu Mia Kalu who are 3 (three) brothers. Kalu died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunnnessa who maintained possession amicably in plot 4613 with respect to 0.15 acres. They sold 0.14½ acres to the plaintiffs by 10 kabalas on 3-10-1989, 11-10-1989, 8-11-1989, 21-12-1989 and delivered possession. Plaintiffs paid rent upon mutation. Defendant 10 appellant claiming under a fraudulent document dated 15-8-1990 threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession for which plaintiff filed Title Suit 324 of 1992 for permanent injunction. The suit was withdrawn after subsequent dispossession on 12-124997. Then plaintiffs filed Title Suit 283 of 1998 for declaration of title and recovery of possession. Suit was dismissed on the finding that plaintiffs have title but their remedy lies in a suit for partition. Hence the suit was filed. 

 5. The case of defendant 3 is that Helu died leaving behind 3(three) sons and 1(one) daughter Alimunnessa. Alimunnessa got 0.20 acres by amicable partition. She sold 0.071/2 acres to defendant 3 Sohrab on 11-3-1984 and delivered possession. Defendants 4 and 10 threatened Sohrab with dispossession. Sohrab then filed Title Suit 357 of 2001 for permanent injunction which was renumbered as Title Suit 180 of 2005 and tagged with Title Suit 177 of 2005 for analogous hearing. 

 6. The case of defendant 4 is that the 4(four) sons and 1(one) daughter of Helu entered into an agreement with defendant 4 on 4-3-1982 in respect of 0.071/2 acres of land and since registration was refused Title Suit 44 of 1985 for Specific Performance of Contract was filed which was decreed on 25-4-1987. She got the document registered through Court on 26- 5-1997 and also got possession. Defendant 3 along with some others had been trying to dispossess defendant 4 for which she filed Title Suit 47 of 2002 for permanent injunction which was renumbered as Title Suit 183 of 2005 and heard analogously with Title Suit 177 of 2005. 

 7. The case of defendant 10 appellant is that KaIlk. Lalu and Helu were owners in possession in the 'Ka' schedule land including 0.35 acres of CS plot 272 of Delpara Mouja. Kalu died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunnessa who by amicable arrangement got the land of Delpara Mouja and accordingly a deed of relinquishment was executed by them on 28-4-1943 disowning partible land. Latifunnessa transferred the land of Delpara to Aslam and others by document dated 21-4-1949, Alimunnessa who is the daughter of Helu and mother of the appellant transferred 0.131/2 acres of land from plot 4613 to this defendant by Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 15-8- 1990 and delivered possession. The maternal uncles of defendant 10 named Shamsuddin, jamaluddin, and 2(two) sons and 2(two) daughters of deceased Alauddin executed a Heba-bil-Ewaz on 2-3-2002 with respect to 0.15 acres in favour of defendant 10. Thus defendant 10 acquired 0.281/2 acres. But since his mother had interest only in 0.0185 acres instead of 0,131/2 acres in plot 4613 he is entitled to 0.1785 acres in total and he prayed saham for such portion. 

 8. The trial Court framed 6(six) issues and decreed Title Suit 177 of 2005 in preliminary form and allotted saham to defendant 10 by judgment and decree dated 28-6-2007. The Court found that the acquisition of land of Delpara Mouja by Karimun and Latifun through amicable arrangement and the execution of nadabi document dated 28-4-1943 by them are absolutely false and Karimun and Latifun had interest in CS plots 4613 and 4614 and also found nobody claimed through Karimun and Latifun except plaintiffs through Exhibits 9-18 which conferred title. The Court also found that the vendor of defendants 3, 4 and 10 named Alimunnessa had interest only in 0.03 acres and the document of defendant 3 being earlier in point of time shall prevail over documents of defendants 4 and 10 and defendant 3 thus claiming under document dated 11-3-1984 got only 0.03 acres instead of 0.071/2 acres and defendant 4 acquired 0.011/2 acres from each of the sons of Helu which in total is 0.06 acres by document dated 26-6-1997 and since the heirs of Helu had remaining interest in 0.15 acres defendant 10 acquired title in the same by Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 2-3-2002. The Court further found that Title Suits 180 and 183 of 2005 filed by defendants 3 and 4 respectively failed due to want of exclusive possession and plaintiffs are entitled to declaration of joint title with the defendants and partition in the land under schedule 'Kha’ of the proceeding referring to order dated 23-1- and defendant 10 is entitled to separate saham 2010 passed in Civil Revision 1129 of 2010 of 0.15 acres of land. 

 10. Both plaintiffs and defendant 10 filed two separate applications for appointment of Advocate Commissioner on 15-8-2007 and those were allowed. Thereafter defendant 4 preferred Title Appeal 302 of 2007 against dismissal of Title Suit 183 of 2005 for which record was called for on 3-10-2007_ Appeal failed and record was received on 25-1-2010 by the lower Court. Plaintiffs paid the commission fee and accordingly Court appointed Mr Md Habibur Rahman as or on 25-1-2010 and fixed the next date on 14-3-2010 for submitting report, Meanwhile on 1-3-2010 which was an off date defendant 10 again filed another application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for direction upon the Commissioner to grant saham in his favour in 0.15 acres from plot 4613 and the application was allowed, Learned Advocate Commissioner filed his report on 22-3.2010 and the next date was fixed on 7-4-2010 for filing objection. But defendant 10 on another off date on 24-3-2010 appeared in the Court to deposit chalan for commission fee and Court appointed Mr Md. Motiar Rahman as Commissioner who was ordered to complete commission according to the prayer made by defendant 10 on 1-3-2010. On 7-4-2010 defendant 10 filed written objection and Commissioner Mr Motiar also filed an application for time for submitting report. Court upon hearing rejected appointment of Mr Motiar and appointed Mr Habibur Rahrnan for holding commission and passed order upon him to deal with commission according to the meaning of the application filed by defendant 10 under Section 151 of the Code and the next date was fixed on 16-5-2010 for submitting report. On 21-4-2010 plaintiffs prayed for stay of the proceeding referring to order dated 23-1-10 and defendant is entitled to separate saham 2010 passed in Civil Revision 1129 of 2010.preferred by defendant 4 and on 16-5-2010 plaintiffs filed an application for status quo in the light of tine order dated 21-3-2010 passed in revision. The Court kept the application with the record and fixed on 27-6-2010 for filing report but Commissioner filed his second report on 24-6-2010. On 6-9-2010 High Court Division called for the record. On 9-4-2019 record was sent back. On 20-5-2019 Court passed order to issue Court notice upon defendants 3, 4, 10 and the left margin of the order shows that the same was issued on 17-6- 2019. On 19-6-2019 Court accepted the second report dated 24-6-2010. On 10-7-2019 plaintiffs filed an application for treating the first report dated 22-3-2010 as part of the decree and to make the preliminary decree final. The application was allowed. The final decree was signed on 24-7-2019. 

 13. Mr Swapan Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents submits that the learned Joint District Judge correctly passed the decree and the report of the Commissioner is evidently clear and valid being made in accordance with the preliminary decree. The written objection dated 74-2010 is made beyond pleading and a new case has been made out which is untenable. He submits that defendant 10 has no allegation that the learned Commissioner did riot serve any notice arid has not gone to the suit land and the report is a mere table work. He then submits that the order 97 dated 15-8-2007 was made not for allotment of 0,15 acres to defendant 10 from plot 4613 but only for allowing the application for appointment of Commissioner. He further submits that the Court notice was duly served upon defendant 10 and in support of his submission he has referred the case of Abdur Rahman and others vs Sultan @ Sultan and others. 35 DLR (AD) 51, He finally submits that since the case of the plaintiffs is not specifically denied in the written statement of defendant 10 he has no reasonable and valid point to object the report and his case in appeal is barred under Order S Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in is support he refers the case of Divisional Estate Officer vs jashimuddin, 24 BLC (AD) 36, 

 15. Plaintiffs claim from the heirs of one of the CS tenants Kalu Mia who got 0.2466 acres in his share and he died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunn.essa and 2(two) brothers Help and Lalu. Accordingly Karimun, Latifun acquired 0.0308 and 0.1233 acres respectively. Plaintiffs purchased the suit land measuring 0.14112 acres from Karimun and Latifun by 10 kabalas Exhibits 9-18 in 1989 and nobody except plaintiffs claims under them in the suit. On the other hand defendant 10 claiming under Helu says that Karimun and Latifun disowned the suit land and got 0.35 acres of Delpara Mouja by amicable arrange-ment and executed a deed of relinquishment on 28-4-1943 Exhibit-B in favour of Helu Mia. Helu died leaving behind 4(four) sons Shamsuddin, Moniruddin, Jamal Uddin, Alauddin and 1(one) daughter Alimunnessa. Alimunnessa got 0.21 acres in plot 4613by amicable partition and executed Heba.-bil-Ewaz dated 15-8-1990 (Exhibit-D) to her son defendant 10 for 0.13½ acres. Subsequently Shamsuddin, Jamal Uddii and heirs of Alauddin executed another Heba-bii-Ewaz (Exhibit-F) on 2-3-2002 in favour of defendant 10 in respect of 0.15 acres. Thus, defendant 10 got 0.28½ acres but ultimately claims 0.1785 acres of land. 

 17. From reading of the judgment passed in Title Suit 283 of 1998 (Exhibit-E) it appears that the acquisition of land in Delpara Mouja by the vendors of plaintiffs and subsequent execution of nadabi deed (Exhibit-B) as claimed by defendant 10 are disbelieved with strong reasons as also is done in the present case. In Exhibit-E defendant 10 claimed 0.131/2 acres by Exhibit-D dated 15-8-1990 arid claimed possession. Now after about 12(twelve) years defendant 10 filed written statement on 24-3- 2002 after 22(twenty two) days of pendente lite execution of Exhibit-F dated 2-3-2002 and disclaimed the land of Exhibit -D except 0.0285 acres and claimed to be owner in possession in 0.1785 acres. It appears that the present suit is the outcome of Exhibit-E and defendant 10 approbates and reprobates according to their desire and convenience. Another important aspect of this case is paragraph 4 of the written objection dated 74-2010 in which defendant 10 made out a third case of sale of 0.24 1/3 acres from plot 4614 by as many as 10 documents from 1986 to 1989 by Monir Uddin who is one of the sons of Helu. Exhibit-8 and Exhibit-E show that although those documents were introduced in written statement and marked in evidence as Exhibit-Cha series in Title Suit 283 of 1998 but those facts are kept hidden in the instant suit because had those documents been introduced defendant 10 surely would have failed to have title by Exhibit-F. The sale of 0.21 acres of plot 4613 from the east side of the suit land by Lalu in favour of the predecessor of defendant 1 is admitted by defendant 10 as apparent from Exhibit-8 and E. Monir Uddin alone sold 0.24 1/3 acres to different persons in possession from plot 4614. Paragraph 160a) of Exhibit-8 shows that Helu's daughter Alimunnessa alone acquired 0.21 acres from plot 4613. She sold 0.07½ acres to defendant 3 Sohrab, Defendant 4 also claimed purchase of 0.07½ acres in execution of a decree from the heirs of Helu. Besides the sale in favour of the plaintiffs stands out. For such reason in the instant case defendant 10 threw out his earlier claim through Exhibit-I) and made out a new case on the strength of a pendente lite Heba-bil-Ewaz (Exhibit-F). We cannot strike the preliminary decree but nevertheless this Court is not unfettered to see and examine the available evidence adduced by the parties and to reach to a satisfactory conclusion and to put an end to the litigation once for all. Exhibit-F appears to have come out of the blue and the transaction seems colourable. It is also hard to believe that all maternal uncles and 4(four) maternal cousins out of love and affection have come forward together and execute a Heba-bil-Ewaz in favour of defendant 10 through Exhibit-F in 2002 during pendency of the suit. 

 18. Suit was decreed in respect of 0.14¼ acres specified by the boundary with the red coloured sketch map as detailed and depicted in the 'ha' schedule. The ordering portion of the judgment shows that preliminary decree of partition is passed in respect of 0.14¼ acres for declaration of title and joint possession of the plaintiffs and defendant 10 gets a separate saham of 0.15 acres of land. The red coloured portion of the sketch map shows the suit land is apparently within plot 4613. Defendant 10 did not prefer any appeal against such decree. There is no scope on part of defendant 10 to deny and challenge such specific portion given in favour of the plaintiffs by the decree passed in preliminary form. Order 103 dated 1-3-2010 shows that defendant 10 filed an application under Section 151 of the Code on the prayer for appointment of Commissioner for getting saham of 0.15 acres from plot 4613 and the application for appointment of Commissioner was allowed. Order 106 dated 24-3-2010 and 107 dated 74-2010 also show that the Court passed order upon the Commissioner to complete his commission work according to the meaning of the prayer made by defendant 10 in his application done under Section 151 of the Code. The Joint District Judge cannot pass such orders which directly go against the preliminary decree itself. Court can make directions in accordance with the principles of equity involved in a partition suit but cannot go behind or beyond the decree for making the same jeopardised and infructuous The above mentioned orders appear to be improper especially when the decree was passed with a clear specification and no appeal is preferred against such decree, Question which has been determined by preliminary decree should be delegated to the Commissioner. 

 20. We have also gone through two commission reports done by the same Advocate Commissioner on 22-3-2010 and 24-6-2010. The language of the two reports are completely same and in the second report it is explained away by the Commissioner that he has got nothing to do in effecting further partition because a report has been earlier filed giving specific saham to the plaintiffs and defendant 10 which is under judicial decision. In the report he clearly speaks that after getting writ he went to the locality on 20-2-2010 at about 10-30 am when plaintiffs were present but despite notice defendant 10 was absent. He also speaks that in effecting partition prior possession has preference for the sake of equitable justice and upon due compliance of judgment and decree along with formal procedures he has allotted 14.25 decimals to the plaintiffs from CS plot 4613 and defendant 10 from plot 4614 though defendant 10 prayed saham in plot 4613 overlapping the saham of the plaintiffs and in the process of effecting partition preliminary decree is complied with. There is no allegation made in the written objection of defendant 10 that the Commissioner did not go to the suit land or the report is a mere table work or he did not start from any fixed pillar or case map or field work is false, Rather defendant 10 says in his objection that he got the suit land by virtue of Exhibit-F dated 2-3-2002 which is 13 (thirteen) years later of plaintiffs' documents Exhibits 9-18 series Plaintiffs' vendors are admitted co-sharers and none of the parties in the suit claims under them. From reading of paragraph 11(Ga) of the written statement of defendants 5 and 6 it appears that the suit land is nal and page 7 of Exhibit-E shows that IRRI paddy is cultivated there, Thus the submission of Mr Dutta that equity has come undone in the instant case because there are buildings standing therein has no basis according to admission of defendant 10 as evident from Exhibit-E. Moreover in view to validate Exhibit-F defendant 10 in paragraphs 42(Ja), (Eno) of the written statement has made out a case of bigger quantum of land with share by implicating the land of Delpara mouja to show that the vendors of Exhibit-F had interest to execute the deed in 2002 during pendency of the suit. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, we are of the view that the Commissioner has correctly prepared the report in accordance with the preliminary decree passed in the original suit and he has not gone behind or beyond the decree where a clear picture of red coloured specification is shown and nobody was aggrieved by such decree. The new case of sale as described in paragraph 4 of the objection being beyond pleading cannot be accepted. The objection appears to be devoid of substance and it does not merit any consideration and hence it is rejected. The report of the Advocate Commissioner is sound and proper and since the same has not violated any established principle of partition and is made in accordance with the preliminary decree, we are not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree.
